--- title: Plot design subtitle: Day 04 title-slide-attributes: data-background-image: ../img/design-plot-icons.png data-background-size: 60% data-background-position: right data-background-opacity: "0.8" data-slide-number: none format: revealjs: incremental: true scrollable: true auto-stretch: false editor_options: chunk_output_type: console --- ## Today - `ggplot2` review - customizations in `ggplot2` - Some guidelines for plot design ## What we know: :::::: columns ::: {.column width="35%"} 1. A basic set of geometries - `geom_point()` - `geom_histogram()` - `geom_boxplot()` - `geom_violin()` - `geom_bar()` ::: ::: {.column width="30%"} 2. How to map variables to aesthetics - `x` and `y` axis - `color` - `shape` - `alpha` - `size` ::: ::: {.column width="30%"} 3. How to change axis labels and titles - `labs()` ::: :::::: ## What next? {background-image="../img/02-ggplot-layers.png" background-size="60%" background-position="right" background-opacity="0.8"} - Setting aesthetics - Using facets - Changing scales - Changing coordinates - Changing themes - Adding annotations ## Where does Carleton land? In 2018, Carleton's in-state tuition was about \$55,000 a year. Was that a lot? And what did Carleton graduates earn? I'd like to make an argument about how Carleton compares to other colleges, using the tuition and pay data from Day 1. ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](slides04_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-1-1.png){width=864} ::: ::: ## Warm Up {.smaller} :::::: columns :::: {.column width="40%"} ::: {.task .nonincremental} 1. Log into maize - If you have to type your PAT in everytime you push to GitHub, follow the directions at [Getting Set up with Git and GitHub](https://stat220-f26.github.io/computing/git-stat220.html#getting-setup-with-git-and-github) #4 to tell RStudio to save your credentials (may or may not work on maize 🤷‍♀️ but definitely works on local installations) 2. Find the `.qmd` template for today at the course website 3. Open it up in maize/Rstudio 4. Work with a neighbor to recreate this graph → ::: :::: ::: {.column width="60%"} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](slides04_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-2-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ::: :::::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ## Polishing plots ::::: columns ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](slides04_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-4-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} We're not quite satisfied.... - I can't tell 50 states apart (and I can't find Carleton!) - The points pile on top of each other - Public and private schools are all mixed together - I don't like the default color scheme - I don't like the gray background ::: ::::: ## *Setting* aesthetics Setting = choosing a certain value for an aesthetic ::: {.cell output-location='column-fragment'} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="6-7"} ggplot(college_pay) + geom_point( aes(x = in_state_tuition, y = mid_career_pay, color = state), alpha = 0.6, size = .5 ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](slides04_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-5-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ## Facets Make "small multiples", where each facet shows a subset of the data ::: {.cell output-location='column-fragment'} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="9"} ggplot(college_pay) + geom_point( aes(x = in_state_tuition, y = mid_career_pay, color = state), alpha = 0.6, size = .5 ) + facet_wrap(vars(type)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](slides04_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-6-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ::: callout-tip You may have seen this before using the syntax `facet_wrap(~type)`. Both work, but `vars()` is the more modern/flexible syntax, so that's what I've used here ::: ## Choose what to color by 50 colors are too many to tell apart. Instead, I made a `group` variable that splits schools into Carleton, other Minnesota colleges, and everywhere else. (We'll learn to make variables like this next week!) ::: {.cell output-location='column-fragment'} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="5"} ggplot(college_pay) + geom_point( aes(x = in_state_tuition, y = mid_career_pay, color = group), alpha = 0.6, size = .5 ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](slides04_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-7-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ## Changing scales ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} scale__() ``` ::: ::::: columns ::: {.column .fragment width="50%"} Examples: - `scale_color_manual()` - `scale_color_brewer()` - `scale_color_viridis_c()` - `scale_shape_manual()` ::: ::: {.column .fragment .nonincremental width="50%"} Recommended reading: - [Using colors in R](http://stat545.com/block018_colors.html) - [Taking control of qualitative colors in ggplot2](http://stat545.com/block019_enforce-color-scheme.html) ::: ::::: ## Example (built-in scale) ::: {.cell output-location='column'} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="9"} ggplot(college_pay) + geom_point( aes(x = in_state_tuition, y = mid_career_pay, color = group), alpha = 0.6, size = 2 ) + scale_color_brewer(palette = "Dark2") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](slides04_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-9-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ## Example (built-in scale) ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} RColorBrewer::display.brewer.all() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](slides04_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-10-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ## Aside: types of color scales ![](../img/color-scales-intro.avif) ::: aside Source: [Datawrapper Blog](https://www.datawrapper.de/blog/which-color-scale-to-use-in-data-vis) ::: ## Example (continuous color scale) Sometimes the variable we color by is numeric, like the percent of graduates with STEM degrees. Then we need a *continuous* color scale. ::: {.cell output-location='column'} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="5,9"} ggplot(college_pay) + geom_point( aes(x = in_state_tuition, y = mid_career_pay, color = stem_percent), alpha = 0.6, size = 2 ) + scale_color_viridis_c() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](slides04_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-11-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ## Example (manual color palette) Let's make Carleton `gold2`, other Minnesota colleges `navyblue`, and everyone else `gray70` ::: {.cell output-location='column'} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="9"} ggplot(college_pay) + geom_point( aes(x = in_state_tuition, y = mid_career_pay, color = group), alpha = 0.6, size = 2 ) + scale_color_manual(values = c("gold2", "navyblue", "gray70")) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](slides04_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-12-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ::: callout-tiip You may have to try a few things to get the colors in the right order ::: ## Can also change non-color scales ::: {.cell output-location='column'} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="10"} ggplot(college_pay) + geom_point( aes(x = in_state_tuition, y = mid_career_pay, color = group), alpha = 0.6, size = 2 ) + scale_color_manual(values = c("gold2", "navyblue", "gray70")) + scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::dollar) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](slides04_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-13-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ## Can also change non-color scales ::: {.cell output-location='column'} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="10"} ggplot(college_pay) + geom_point( aes(x = in_state_tuition, y = mid_career_pay, color = group), alpha = 0.6, size = 2 ) + scale_color_manual(values = c("gold2", "navyblue", "gray70")) + scale_x_log10() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](slides04_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-14-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ## Can also change non-color scales ::: {.cell output-location='column'} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="10"} ggplot(college_pay) + geom_point( aes(x = in_state_tuition, y = mid_career_pay, color = group), alpha = 0.6, size = 2 ) + scale_color_manual(values = c("gold2", "navyblue", "gray70")) + scale_x_reverse() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](slides04_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-15-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ## Changing Themes **Theme:** The non-data ink on your plots ::::: columns ::: {.column .nonincremental width="30%"} - background - tick marks - grid lines - font - legend position - legend appearance ::: ::: {.column width="70%"} ::: {.cell layout-ncol="2"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](slides04_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-16-1.png){width=384} ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](slides04_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-16-2.png){width=384} ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](slides04_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-16-3.png){width=384} ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](slides04_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-16-4.png){width=384} ::: ::: ::: ::::: ## Prepackaged themes ::::: columns ::: {.column .nonincremental width="50%"} `ggplot2` themes - `theme_grey()` - `theme_bw()` - `theme_linedraw()` - `theme_light()` - `theme_dark()` - `theme_minimal()` - `theme_classic()` - `theme_void()` - `theme_test()` ::: ::: {.column .nonincremental width="50%"} `ggthemes` themes - `theme_clean()` - `theme_economist()` - `theme_excel()` - `theme_fivethirtyeight()` - `theme_gdocs()` - `theme_solarized()` - `theme_stata()` - `theme_tufte()` - `theme_wsj()` - And more! ::: ::::: ## Using a prepackaged theme {.middle} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="6"} ggplot(data = ) + ( mapping = aes() ) + + theme_() ``` ::: ## Try it Apply `theme_light()` to the scatterplot ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](slides04_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-18-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ## Even *more* customizations - Move legend - Clean up labels and title - Format the axis labels - Annotations ## ![](../img/ggplot2-theme-elements-reference-v2.png) ::: {.aside} Source: [Isabella Benabaye](https://isabella-b.com/blog/ggplot2-theme-elements-reference/) ::: ## `?theme` ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} theme(line, rect, text, title, aspect.ratio, axis.title, axis.title.x, axis.title.x.top, axis.title.x.bottom, axis.title.y, axis.title.y.left, axis.title.y.right, axis.text, axis.text.x, axis.text.x.top, axis.text.x.bottom, axis.text.y, axis.text.y.left, axis.text.y.right, axis.ticks, axis.ticks.x, axis.ticks.x.top, axis.ticks.x.bottom, axis.ticks.y, axis.ticks.y.left, axis.ticks.y.right, axis.ticks.length, axis.line, axis.line.x, axis.line.x.top, axis.line.x.bottom, axis.line.y, axis.line.y.left, axis.line.y.right, legend.background, legend.margin, legend.spacing, legend.spacing.x, legend.spacing.y, legend.key, legend.key.size, legend.key.height, legend.key.width, legend.text, legend.text.align, legend.title, legend.title.align, legend.position, legend.direction, legend.justification, legend.box, legend.box.just, legend.box.margin, legend.box.background, legend.box.spacing, panel.background, panel.border, panel.spacing, panel.spacing.x, panel.spacing.y, panel.grid, panel.grid.major, panel.grid.minor, panel.grid.major.x, panel.grid.major.y, panel.grid.minor.x, panel.grid.minor.y, panel.ontop, plot.background, plot.title, plot.subtitle, plot.caption, plot.tag, plot.tag.position, plot.margin, strip.background, strip.background.x, strip.background.y, strip.placement, strip.text, strip.text.x, strip.text.y, strip.switch.pad.grid, strip.switch.pad.wrap, ..., complete = FALSE, validate = TRUE) ``` ::: ::: aside To see examples in action, see ["Theme Elements"](https://ggplot2-book.org/themes#sec-theme-elements) of the ggplot2 book ::: ## Move the legend ::: {.cell output-location='column'} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="11-13"} ggplot(college_pay) + geom_point( aes(x = in_state_tuition, y = mid_career_pay, color = group), alpha = 0.6, size = 2 ) + scale_color_manual(values = c("gold2", "navyblue", "gray70")) + theme_minimal() + theme( legend.position = "top" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](slides04_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-21-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ## Clean up labels and title ::: {.cell output-location='column'} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="14-19"} ggplot(college_pay) + geom_point( aes(x = in_state_tuition, y = mid_career_pay, color = group), alpha = 0.6, size = 2 ) + scale_color_manual(values = c("gold2", "navyblue", "gray70")) + theme_minimal() + theme( legend.position = "top" ) + labs( x = "In-state tuition", y = "Median mid-career pay", color = "", title = "Carleton: top 4% in tuition, top 13% in pay" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](slides04_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-22-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ## Remove minor gridlines ::: {.cell output-location='column'} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="13"} ggplot(college_pay) + geom_point( aes(x = in_state_tuition, y = mid_career_pay, color = group), alpha = 0.6, size = 2 ) + scale_color_manual(values = c("gold2", "navyblue", "gray70")) + theme_minimal() + theme( legend.position = "top", panel.grid.minor = element_blank() ) + labs( x = "In-state tuition", y = "Median mid-career pay", color = "", title = "Carleton: top 4% in tuition, top 13% in pay" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](slides04_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-23-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ## Format the axes ::: {.cell output-location='column'} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="10-11"} ggplot(college_pay) + geom_point( aes(x = in_state_tuition, y = mid_career_pay, color = group), alpha = 0.6, size = 2 ) + scale_color_manual(values = c("gold2", "navyblue", "gray70")) + scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::dollar) + scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::dollar) + theme_minimal() + theme( legend.position = "top", panel.grid.minor = element_blank() ) + labs( x = "In-state tuition", y = "Median mid-career pay", color = "", title = "Carleton: top 4% in tuition, top 13% in pay" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](slides04_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-24-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ## Add an annotation ::: {.cell output-location='column'} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="23-36"} ggplot(college_pay) + geom_point( aes(x = in_state_tuition, y = mid_career_pay, color = group), alpha = 0.6, size = 2 ) + scale_color_manual(values = c("gold2", "navyblue", "gray70")) + scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::dollar) + scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::dollar) + theme_minimal() + theme( legend.position = "top", panel.grid.minor = element_blank() ) + labs( x = "In-state tuition", y = "Median mid-career pay", color = "", title = "Carleton: top 4% in tuition, top 13% in pay" ) + annotate("point", x = 54759, y = 109900, shape = 1, size = 7, stroke = 1.2, col = "gold4") + annotate("text", x = 52500, y = 109900, label = "Carleton", hjust = 1, fontface = "bold", col = "gold4") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](slides04_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-25-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ::: callout-tip I had to look these values up in the data, and try a few different combinations to get it to look OK ::: ## Increase text size ::: {.cell output-location='column'} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="12,36"} ggplot(college_pay) + geom_point( aes(x = in_state_tuition, y = mid_career_pay, color = group), alpha = 0.6, size = 2 ) + scale_color_manual(values = c("gold2", "navyblue", "gray70")) + scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::dollar) + scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::dollar) + theme_minimal(base_size = 20) + theme( legend.position = "top", panel.grid.minor = element_blank() ) + labs( x = "In-state tuition", y = "Median mid-career pay", color = "", title = "Carleton: top 4% in tuition, top 13% in pay" ) + annotate("point", x = 54759, y = 109900, shape = 1, size = 7, stroke = 1.2, col = "gold4") + annotate("text", x = 52500, y = 109900, label = "Carleton", hjust = 1, fontface = "bold", size = 6, col = "gold4") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](slides04_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-26-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ## <script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
